title: Music21 Chord Payload
description: Roman-numeral chord labels and their local keys, one row per chord with parallel-array columns. Based on the Beethoven Piano Sonata Functional Harmony (BPS-FH) dataset. Used with quarters_interval.float or quarters_interval.fraction extents.

value.description: Roman-numeral labels in music21 RomanNumeral figure syntax, as a grammar rather than an enumeration: an optional repeatable flat 'b' or sharp '#' prefix, a degree I II III IV V VI VII in upper or lower case (never mixed), an optional quality mark ('-' diminished and '=' half-diminished as spelled by BPS-FH, '+' augmented, music21's 'o' diminished and 'ø' half-diminished), and an optional figure 6, 53, 63, 64, 7, 65, 43, 42, 9, 11 or 13; the augmented-sixth names It, Fr, Ger and Sw with an optional figure 6, 53, 43, 65 or 7, plus the BPS-FH spellings It+6, Fr+6 and Gr+6; the Neapolitan N with an optional figure 6, 64 or 53; and the cadential Cad64. Any of these may be followed by a '/'-separated chain of secondary chords; a secondary degree always follows a '/'. The grammar accepts all 197 distinct RN strings of the 11,478 BPS-FH chords.xlsx rows once the BPS-FH reader has normalized that dataset's three malformed labels (Vi/III -> VI/III, V7IV -> V7/IV, vii-65V -> vii-65/V). Out of scope: bracketed alterations such as V[no5] or V7[no3], music21's '-' accidental prefix (-VI; BPS-FH spells it bVI), the BPS-FH abbreviation 'Gr' outside 'Gr+6', and any check of harmonic correctness.

key.description: Local tonics in music21 notation: A-G for major or a-g for minor, optionally followed by one or more sharps '#' or one or more flats '-'. BPS-FH spells sharps with '+' (e.g. C+, f+); the BPS-FH reader translates '+' to '#' before constructing this payload.
